newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-ULLRICH ENDS GERMAN TOUR DROUGHT.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-ULLRICH ENDS GERMAN TOUR DROUGHT.

text.p: Jan Ullrich's Tour de France triumph on Sunday ended a German drought dating back to the very beginning of the world's premier cycle race.

In the 94 years since the first Tour, few Germans have been to the fore but many observers regard the 23-year-old Rostock-born champion as the natural heir to another young German star, Dietrich Thurau.
Thurau was 22 when he took the Tour by storm in 1977 with six stage victories and possession of the coveted yellow jersey for 15 days before succumbing to the tenacity of Frenchman Bernard Thevenet.
Altogether nine Germans have worn the leader's yellow before Ullrich, with Klaus-Peter Thaler the last, for two days in 1978.
Germany's best result came in 1932 when Kurt Stoepel finished second, 24 minutes behind French winner Andre Leducq but there has been success elsewhere.
Rudi Altig, who as points champion took the Tour de France green jersey in 1962, won the Tour of Spain the same year, while Rolf Wolfshohl won the Spanish race three years later.
The end of the long wait for another major success was marked by the thousands of Germans who flocked across the border to Colmar to cheer Ullrich home in Wednesday's 17th stage.
Having sprung to prominence with a brilliant time trial last year, Ullrich went on to finish second overall behind his team leader Bjarne Riis of Denmark.
He began the 1997 Tour by supporting Riis, a rider he respects highly, but was torn in the Pyrenees between helping the troubled Dane or going out on his own.
The German's doubts held him back for only one day, however, as after a team meeting he stormed into the lead with a brilliant stage victory in Andorra.
There he proved superior to two proven climbers, French King of the Mountains Richard Virenque and Marco Pantani of Italy.
They were on the podium on the Champs Elysees in second and third place respectively on Sunday but it was Ullrich -- and Germany -- proudly on top.
